test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 26 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the radius and height of a right circular cylinder are 21 cm and 5 cm, respectively, then the total surface area of the cylinder is (use \pi =(22)/(7) ):
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area of cylinder = 2 × π × r(r + h)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 21 × 26

⇒ TSA = 44 × 3 × 26 = 3432 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3432 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius (r) = 21 cm

Height (h) = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder = 2 × π × r × (r + h)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/897e06aa8b405cc1e9332d33acca26de5b8ffdbf38d13fc75e95135b25fc7ce9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (22/7) × 21 × (21 + 5)

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × 22 × 3 × 26

⇒ Total Surface Area = 44 × 78

⇒ Total Surface Area = 3432 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3432 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of a Cylinder

The curved surface area includes only the lateral surface: CSA = 2 × π × r × h.

Volume of a Cylinder

The capacity of a right circular cylinder: Volume = π × r² × h.

Total Surface Area of a Cone

TSA of a right circular cone = π × r(l + r), where l is the slant height (√(r² + h²)).
